messages:
maya: heads-up, trying to onboard hf repo 'oxford-kwai' for evals, ran into trust_remote_code issues
alex: what happened? brief pls
maya: conversion fails on redwood-convert with: 
```
ValueError: auto_map failed: ClassNotFoundError for 'KwaiModel'
Hint: model uses custom architecture with trust_remote_code
```
alex: is this one of the repos that ships custom tokenizers/configs?
maya: yes. config.json has `architectures` set to a nonstandard name and special_tokens_map missing `<pad>`/`<bos>`. tokenizer has `added_tokens.json` too
rachel: do we have a canonical fallback for auto_map? we usually prefer not to enable `trust_remote_code` for security reasons
maya: tried `--trust-remote-code` and conversion proceeds but decoder outputs mismatch with hf raw for long-context tests
tony: mismatch how severe? numbers?\maya: LAMBADA acc drops from 0.42 (hf fp16) to 0.31 (redwood int8 w/ autoconvert + trust_remote_code) on initial run. PIQA also regressed ~5 pts\maya: logs show tokenizer mapping difference: hf uses `special_tokens_map: {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}` but redwood-convert produced `<s>` mapped to `<start>` which breaks chat templates
bench-bot: auto-bench job queued: https://ci/bench/1965432111 (will post full table) :timer_clock:
alex: could be two issues: (1) autoloaded custom class implements nonstandard `prepare_inputs_for_generation`, (2) tokenizer special token names mismatch. Either can break generation conditioning
rachel: recommended approach: 1) vendor a minimal wrapper class with same API but no arbitrary top-level code, 2) augment config.json to include `architectures` canonical mapping and `tokenizer_class` fallback, 3) add explicit `special_tokens_map` before conversion
maya: attempted 1 — added stub KwaiModel in repo with class that delegates to HF weights, convert runs, and output aligns for short seqs but still fails on prefix caching under continuous batching
ton y: small typo in name? (tony)\tony: oops. re: prefix caching — custom `past_key_values` handling is different in that model. We need to ensure `use_cache` hooks map to runtime API. Suggest adding simple shim in wrapper: `def prepare_inputs_for_generation(self, *args, **kwargs): return super().prepare_inputs_for_generation(*args, **kwargs)`
maya: created shim, rerun quantize int8 with QAT-like tweaks, LAMBADA up to 0.38 now but still shy of hf fp16. quality/regression alerts currently firing in console
rachel: for immediate unblockedness, can we route production inference to hosted hf for this model and keep redwood-dev blocked until we validate?\maya: yes can do route policy: `route: prefer_hf_if_trustrc` temporarily. Will also open eval PR with manual prompt set and seed for deterministic checks
alex: also log the full `tokenizer.json` and `special_tokens_map` in the artifact so we can diff easily. put that in the bench job
infra-bot: note: enabling trust_remote_code for convert requires security review ticket #SEC-4114 before prod use
maya: filed SEC ticket, linked PR to the repo, and uploaded artifact: s3://redwood-ci/1965432111/artifacts/tokenizer_diff.json
bench-bot: bench finished: LAMBADA: hf-fp16=0.42 | redwood-convert-int8-trustrc=0.38 | redwood-convert-int8-stubwrap=0.40. Full CSV attached to the job
alex: OK. next steps: (a) vendor minimal deterministic wrapper, (b) harmonize special tokens and chat template mapping (`system` -> `<s>`, `assistant`->`</s>`), (c) run ablation for quantization knobs, (d) update onboarding doc with checklist for trust_remote_code models
maya: will do. tagging @rachel for rollout decision and @tony for runtime shim review
rachel: thanks. please keep thread updated, push small PRs. :thumbsup:
